speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I am Dr. Agent; since you are a newborn, I will rely on your parents for your medical history. How long has your baby been alive, and have you noticed any specific symptoms like jaundice, breathing difficulties, or feeding problems?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, female. The patient is a 3000-g (6.6-lb) female newborn delivered at term to a 23-year-old primigravida mother. The mother reports having had no prenatal care, and immunization records for the newborn are not available.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that history. Given the lack of prenatal care and immunizations, are you noticing any signs of infection such as fever, poor feeding, lethargy, or bulging fontanelles? Also, have you observed any respiratory distress like grunting, flaring, or retractions?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Continuous heart murmur. I also have Bluish macules on the skin that do not blanch with pressure, Cloudy lenses in both eyes noticed upon examination, Failure to pass auditory screening tests.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: DiGeorge Syndrome (22q11.2 deletion syndrome).

The combination of a continuous heart murmur (suggesting patent ductus arteriosus), blanching-resistant skin lesions (nevus flammeus/infantile hemangiomas), and cataracts with hearing loss is highly characteristic of this condition. REQUEST IMAGES: Echocardiogram and fundoscopic exam.
